# Placement {.transition}

## Placement (SAS Policy in Global Languages)

::: {layout="[[-1], [1], [-1]]"}

All students (heritage or non-heritage) who wish to enroll in classes in Spanish and Portuguese must take a placement exam IF they have taken two or more years of Spanish in high school. 

:::

## Placement (SAS Policy in Global Languages)

Exceptions to this policy:

- Less than two years can take 101 and 102 
- Transfer students will start at the next level
- Students that have received credit for AP Spanish and whose results are listed in DN
- No native students should be registered in language classes (send them to me or to Luis)

## Placement (SAS Policy in Global Languages)

- Placement exam closes **MONDAY, September 9th at 3 PM**. It reopens October 21st, 2024

- Where can students find their placement results? Go to **MY COURSE LIST** tab in Degree Navigator.

- **PLACEMENT** results are listed at the bottom of the page





# Heritage/non-heritage students {.transition}

## Heritage/non-heritage students

- If you think you have a heritage student in a non-heritage class, contact Sara immediately
  - Non heritage sequence: 101, 102 (or 121), 131, 132, 203, 204
  - Heritage sequence: 139, 201, 202.  

## Heritage/non-heritage students

- If a heritage student is struggling in 139, let Sara know immediately. 
- The student may need to go to 121 and then take 139
- Heritage and non-heritage students may take 203/204 OR 201/202 during the same semester. 
- They will be able to register on their own for 201/203 but will need an override for 202/204
- 201 is not offered for the Fall 2024 semester, therefore Heritage students can register for 203 equivalent





# Rutgers employees {.transition}

## Rutgers employees

- State employees: if you have an emergency, please let Sara know. She will report to me or Nuria
- E-mail
  - Affiliated with the University
  - E-mail policy: please answer messages within 24 hours except on weekends, be sure to make it explicit that it will take you longer
  - Do not give any grades via e-mail
  - Follow netiquette when addressing your students

## Rutgers employees

- FERPA: You cannot discuss any academic issues with the parents of a student unless the student shows written consent authorizing the parents to get information

- [Title IX Policy and Grievance Procedures](https://uec.rutgers.edu/wp-content/uploads/60-1-33-current-4.pdf)

- Professional development: must attend all meetings, trainings, workshops


## Rutgers employees

- Academic Integrity: [Current Rutgers University Academic Integrity Policy](http://nbacademicintegrity.rutgers.edu/home/academic-integrity-policy/)

- If a student is MIA more than three consecutive times without an excuse please send the student a note and CC me 

- If there are no final exams in the course, instructor must turn in their grades 72 hours after their last class meeting


# Academics {.transition}

## How to be flexible and maintain accountability {.smaller}

- If a student cannot maintain pace of the course, it is best that s/he drops the course (see next slide for important Fall 2024 Dates)
- Be sure to file a warning grades when appropriate (you will receive a message from Registrars during week 8)
- Office hours: on campus or video conference at least two hours per class per week
- Accommodations for disabilities 
- Online policy for deadlines
- NO instructor should move the deadline to the reading day to accommodate students. - Instead, the student will receive a new deadline during exam week in consultation with Sara 
- "T" grades are for students that are missing specific components of the course, not for a student that is missing over 75% of the course requirements


## Important Fall 2023 Dates {.smaller}

- Sept. 2: Labor Day - University closed
- Sept. 3: Classes begin
- Sept. 12: Last day to drop without a “W”, last day to add a course
- Oct. 7-18: Warning grade period
- Oct. 21: Spring term schedule visible
- Oct. 28: Last day to withdraw from individual classes with a "W"
- Nov. 11: Registration for Spring term starts
- Dec. 11: Last day of classes
- Dec. 12-13: Reading Days
- Dec. 16-23: Final Exam period
